## Introduction

What is the central question that motivates your analysis? Who may this analysis benefit? Are you trying to train a model, test a hypothesis, classify objects apart? Why? This has to be written with proper grammar and syntax: sentences, paragraphs, and a narrative structure.

The basis of what we are attempting to research is to determine the cause and potential improvement of the racial wealth gap throughout the United States. Specifically, we want to determine if there is any relationship between the racial wealth gap and educational accessibility throughout recent years.

We believe conducting research into this topic will assist in determining future decisions regarding educational needs and allocation of government spending to potentially provide assistance to those in a lower income bracket to have a better opportunity to get the education they need for themselves and, if in families, their children.

## Data

What is the data available for performing the analysis? Where did you retrieve these data from? What are the variables and number of observations available? What steps where performed to clean the data? If the data is obtained via randomized simulations, clarify the data generating procedure.

The data we are using comes from the United States Federal Reserve Board, downloaded from the offical website at https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/z1/dataviz/dfa/index.html? (DFA) and https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/scfindex.htm? (SCF). The DFA data set contains information from the Distributional Financial Accounts, tracked by the Federal Reserve. The SCF data set contains information from the Survey of Consumer Finances, collected by the Federal Reserve. The downloadable file for both are folders containing multiple data sets. The SCF folder contains 31 separate files and the DFA folder contains 27 separate files. As part of our projet, we will be loading singluar files into the workspace as needed to view the data.

For the current visualizations, we compared racial categories and net worth, as well as income before taxes. Using a boxplot, we could see that throughout the years analyzed, white people earned more than any other race. Though this is just a view of net worth compared to race, we can infer that there is a consistent racial wealth gap. For the next steps of our project, we can compare other financial categories to race, like debts and assets.
